'''''Fallopia baldschuanica''''' ([[Synonym (taxonomy)|syn.]] ''Polygonum baldschuanicum'') is an Asian species of flowering plant in the [[Polygonaceae|knotweed family]] known by several common names, including '''Russian-vine''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> '''Bukhara fleeceflower''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=POBA3|taxon=Polygonum baldschuanicum|accessdate=19 January 2016}}</ref>  '''Chinese fleecevine''', '''mile-a-minute''' and '''silver lace vine'''. It is native to Asia (China, Russia, Kazakhstan, etc.),<ref name=gwin>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=242321901 Flora of China, ''Fallopia aubertii'' (L. Henry) Holub, 1971.  <big>木藤首乌</big> mu teng shou wu ]</ref> and is growing wild in parts of Europe and North and Central America as an [[introduced species]].<ref name=gwen/><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=fallopia+baldschuanica Altervista Flora Italiana, ''Fallopia baldschuanica'' (Regel) Holub]</ref><ref name=gwin/>

Some authors split the species in two, referring to the Chinese populations as ''[[Fallopia aubertii]]'' and the Russian and Central Asian species as ''F. baldschuanica.''<ref name=gwin/>

''Fallopia baldschuanica'' is grown as an [[ornamental plant]] for its flower-laced vines. The white flowers are decorative and provide [[nectar]] and pollen for the [[honey bee]].<ref name=gwen/><ref name=gwin/> As it is fast-growing, it is used as cover for unsightly fences and other garden structures.  It can become [[invasive species|invasive]], however.{{citation needed|date=December 2022}}

==Description==

''Fallopia baldschuanica'' is a vining plant with woody, climbing stems  at least {{convert|10|m|ft|0}} in length. The pointed oval or nearly triangular leaves are up to {{convert|10|cm|in|0}} long and borne on [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]]. The [[inflorescence]] is an open array of narrow, branching, drooping or spreading clusters of white flowers, each cluster reaching a maximum of {{convert|15|cm|in|0}} long. Flowers hang on short [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicels]]. Each five-lobed flower is just under a centimeter long and white to greenish or pale pink, sometimes turning bright pink as the fruit develops. The fruit is a shiny black [[achene]] about {{convert|2|mm|in|frac=64}} wide.<ref name=gwen>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=242100054 Flora of North America, ''Fallopia baldschuanica'' (Regel) Holub, 1971. Bukhara fleeceflower, mile-a-minute vine ]</ref>
